newsitem.title: INDIA: India JM Mutual Fund hikes dividend on two schemes.
newsitem.headline: India JM Mutual Fund hikes dividend on two schemes.

text.p: India's JM Mutual Fund said on Wednesday it raised dividend on two of its schemes for the year ended March 31, 1997, despite an eight percent fall of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) sensitive index on Monday which hurt net asset values.

JM Balanced Fund stepped up dividend to 17 percent from 16 percent in the previous year and JM Liquid Fund raised dividend to 18 percent from 16 percent, Nimesh Kampani, chairman of the JM Group told a news conference on Wednesday.
"NAVs (net asset values) of mutual funds fell by 75 paise to one rupee on March 31 following the 300 points stock market fall (on that day at the Bombay Stock Exchange)," Kampani said.
Two other funds of JM, JM Equity Fund and JM Tax Cover both announced a 6.0 percent dividend for the year ended March 31.

Kampani said the fund followed a strategy of minimising loss in a bad market as opposed to the normal strategy of maximising profits. "Protection of capital is becoming very important to the investor these days," he said.
JM's strategy of concentrating more on the debt market in its liquid and balanced funds paid off, Kampani said.
JM Mutual Fund has managed funds for 1.75 billion rupees during the year under its various schemes, he said.
